cards.text: A new king takes the throne in Jerusalem: Jotham, twenty-five years old. His mother is Jerushah, daughter of Zadok. Twenty-five and running a KINGDOM, while it takes me three tries just to set an oven timer.

cards.question: King Jotham reigns in Jerusalem for ___ years.

cards.text: So how does Jotham do? He does what's right in the eyes of the LORD, just like his father Uzziah. Good start, friend. GOOD start.

cards.question: Jotham follows his father Uzziah in doing right. But there's one place Uzziah went that Jotham does not enter. Where?
King Jotham does right before the LORD, but the people of Judah still behave ___.

cards.text: Then Jotham rebuilds the Upper Gate of the house of the LORD and works extensively on the wall at the hill of Ophel. EXTENSIVELY, friend. That's a man who did NOT hit the snooze button.

cards.question: Jotham keeps building, with cities in the hill country of Judah. Out in the forests, what does he put up?

cards.text: Then the builder goes to battle. Jotham wages war against the king of the Ammonites.

cards.question: King Jotham goes to war against the king of the Ammonites. How does it end?

cards.text: And that year the Ammonites pay up: a hundred talents of silver, ten thousand cors of wheat and ten thousand cors of barley. TEN THOUSAND cors of wheat? I bake for a living, friend, and I have NEVER seen that much flour in one place.

cards.question: The Ammonites pay Jotham the same silver, wheat and barley again in the second and third years.

cards.text: So Jotham grows powerful, and the text tells us exactly why. Lean in, friend, because this is the whole recipe right here.

answers.text: He set his ways before the LORD his God
He made peace with the kings around him
He trusted in the size of his army

cards.text: The rest of what Jotham did, all his wars and his ways, is written in the Book of the Kings of Israel and Judah. All his WARS? We heard about ONE! The rest are in that book, friend.
Twenty-five when he became king, sixteen years reigning in Jerusalem. Then Jotham rests with his fathers.

cards.question: King Jotham is buried in the City of ___.
After Jotham, his son Ahaz reigns in his place.

findings.problem: The question says Uzziah went into the temple. That fact is not in this passage. It comes from 2 Chronicles 26:16, but the card gives no reference for it. No earlier card sets it up either, so the baker has nothing to reason from.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The question reads 'King Jotham does right before the LORD, but the people of Judah still behave ___.' The words 'but' and 'still' signal a contrast. That rules out the two positive wrong answers, 'faithfully' and 'humbly', so only 'corruptly' fits.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: 'Then the builder goes to battle' says the war came after the building work. The text only lists the building (vv. 3–4) and the war (v. 5) one after the other. It never says which came first.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The right answer says 'He set his ways before the LORD his God.' The BSB says 'ordered his ways.' 'Set his ways' is close to the phrase 'set in his ways,' which means stubborn. That changes what the text calls it.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The right answer is the only one that mentions the LORD and the only one in Bible phrasing ('before the LORD his God'). It stands out from the two wrong answers.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.
